look_here_first: Look along the stem first: tiny narrow, densely overlapping, leathery leaves, with a raised midrib and paired longitudinal grooves on the upper face. Confirm the woody/perennial base and, at fruiting, a single series of roughly 24–26 white barbellate pappus bristles; unlike the tiny pappus rings of C. effusa and C. bellidifolia.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Master Pool personal source, accepted identity reviewed 2026-10-10; Texas state-native per POWO but county native threshold unresolved.

morphology_keys.habit: Low woody-based or rhizomatous perennial with branched hairy, sometimes glandular stems; usually a small clump.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate, densely overlapping, narrow and firm, commonly 2–10 mm long; upper surface with strongly raised midnerve and paired longitudinal grooves (FNA key).
morphology_keys.heads: Small solitary terminal radiate heads with white to pinkish rays, yellow disk florets and often reddish-tipped phyllaries; ray color changes and is not diagnostic.
morphology_keys.fruits: Cypselae carry one series of usually 24–26 (occasionally 20–30) white barbellate pappus bristles (FNA key).
best_field_traits: Examine basal and stem leaves including overlap and blade bases
Examine mature cypsela pappus with magnification

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. effusa has broad flat non-overlapping lower leaves and a minute pappus ring; C. bellidifolia is a taprooted annual with flat leaves and a tiny ring. C. hersheyi also has overlapping leathery leaves but much shorter stems and a two-series pappus with only about five long inner bristles plus outer scales.
comparisons.cautions: Leaf crowding is most useful with pappus confirmation; a flowering photograph cannot prove pappus number. Color and size alone are insufficient.
